INTERNSHIP INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
FISERV
Prachiti Barge, CS, B.Tech 2019-2023
Round 1: Group Discussion (25 minutes)
We had given names in the sheet circulated by TPO when fiserv came, we (at least I was)
were expecting a coding test announcement after our MST week, but suddenly in the week
after MST at 29.09.21, Wednesday evening they sent a shortlist for Group Discussion round
in which my name was there...I guess they took almost everybody that satisfied their CGPA
criteria, I mean that would have probably been their first filtering criteria, so almost
everyone who gave names were shortlisted and they had divided us into groups of 6 for the
GD, which was to be held the next day i.e 30.09.21, Thursday. This was totally unexpected
because I hadn’t heard of any company conducting GDs for internships. I had absolutely no
idea of how a GD takes place, but then after discussion with friends and seniors, I prepared
for some very commonly asked topics (here, by prepared I mean just read about those
topics briefly :p)
Next day, our timing for GD was 10:00 am to 10.30 am. We were asked to join 20 minutes
before but the lady on the GD Panel who was conducting our GD didn’t come till around
10.20 am. Then, at 10.20 he came and gave us 2 topics out of which we had to choose one
for our GD.
The 2 topics were -1)  Women Empowerment and Gender Justice , 2) Merits and Demerits
of Cashless Economy
We chose the first one i.e  Women Empowerment and Gender Justice. We were given 1-2
minutes to think and then one of us started. In general, everyone covered points like
growing involvement of women in Tech, various special programmes launched by various
companies for the same, examples of leading women in Tech (everyone stressed more on
women in tech specifically since we are all related to tech I suppose, i.e we are all
engineers)

Education of women/girl children in rural areas, schemes or actions taken by the
government to ensure that a girl child gets education, someone also spoke about the
recent Taliban issue. People also spoke about the other (negative) side, i.e strength
comparison men vs women, are women capable enough to carry huge responsibilities w.r.t
their physical strengths, etc. it ended with one of us concluding the GD.
Tips for GD out of my experience:
-
Keep updates of what is going around you in the world, at least the hot topics.
-
In the process of interview preparation, one may ignore reading news, latest
technologies, inventions etc (even if it is your daily habit, we tend to give all of this a
very low priority in life) but don’t do that, you never know when that knowledge will
come handy especially in situations like this when GDs are announced at 11th hr.
-
There is no particular order that is followed in a GD, so don’t wait for anyone to call
out your name to speak, just say your name and put your point forward.
-
Read the basic manners and etiquettes to be followed in a GD from internet (bohot
sites available hai iss sab ke liye)
-
If you are like me (who is not a daily reader xD) then google most frequently asked
topics in a GD, with answers mil jaata hai net pe
-
Some very common topics include - Covid-19 impact (on various sectors, primarily
financial, banking sector and economy if its a bank) on India and globally,
Cryptocurrencies, future of blockchain, Women rights and empowerment, recent
hot incidents, etc
-
If you cannot start the discussion, start in the middle and summarize if possible
(actually, it okay if you neither start nor summarize (I didn’t do both xD) but try to)
-
If you don’t have any points to speak of then at least mention examples that would
support  certain points
-
Try not directly cutting someone off when someone is speaking, it pisses off the
recruiter. Once someone has  made a point, you can pick up from there.
-
Make sure you are making eye contact with the person you are speaking to.
2

-
Lastly, keep your voice firm and confident, yet humble, people may try to cut each
other off, don't become annoyed stay calm and make sure to grab any opportunity
to speak
44 people were shortlisted for the Technical round of interview which was held next day
Round 2: Technical Interview (30-35 minutes)
The interviewer was a lady and from her face, she seemed to be a little strict, but I kept
myself calm. She first asked me to introduce myself. Keep this ready (memorize it if
required) as it is almost asked in every interview. She probably had my resume in front of
her, so he started asking me questions regarding the things I had mentioned in my resume.
I had done an internship in blockchain development, so she asked me to describe my
experience and highlight a few points from my research as it was kind of a research intern.
She was asking me follow up questions on whatever I included in my explanation (for ex. I
mentioned Cryptographic hash functions, so she asked me what are hash functions)
Then she went on to my projects and asked a few questions regarding my project, but
those questions weren’t very complicated.
She then asked me to explain the concept of Object Oriented Programming. This is a very
important topic and it is highly recommended that you are thorough with OOPS. I had
revised OOPS recently so I was quite confident and started explaining to her all 4 pillars
with a real life example. I first explained the need of that pillar and then what it is and how
it increases the efficiency of our code. As I finished with Abstraction and Encapsulation, she
probably wasn’t satisfied so for more clarity she asked me the difference between
abstraction and encapsulation, I explained her again by highlighting the difference, then I
continued with polymorphism and when I started with inheritance she stopped me and
asked me to write a code in any language I preferred that uses all the concepts of OOPS.
She gave me 1-1.5 minute to write the code on simple notepad, after 1 min she asked me if
I was done, but I was left with inheritance, so I told her that I am just left with inheritance
and I asked for some more time, but she denied she just told me read out whatever class,
properties, methods I had written and I explained her my code and also told her what I had
in mind for implementing inheritance (as I didn’t have time to write code for that). She
seemed to be satisfied with my explanation.
3

The OOPS discussion lasted long.
Then, she asked me if I was familiar with SQL, she probably knew I was, as I had mentioned
relevant courses in my resume where I had mentioned DBMS. She then gave (rather
narrated) me a schema design and asked me to write a query to change the column name
in the schema design she gave, I immediately wrote the query and read it for her and she
said okay. Then she asked me what an index in SQL was. I had not revised this, so I couldn’t
remember it at that time, so I told her that I don’t remember it now and that I'll have to
brush up on this topic. She was like okay no problem.
Lastly, she told me to revise the topics I am left with and try to understand concepts
properly ( When she said this, I thought that she wouldn’t have been satisfied with my
answers :/ though I was satisfied with my performance, it was at least better than what I
had expected )
Though there were a few things I didn’t know, I told her honestly and kept myself calm and
composed, with that smile on my face throughout.
This was the end of the technical round, we had to wait for almost 2 hrs for the shortlist for
the next managerial round to come. Managerial round shortlist was not sent at once; they
first sent a list of 6-7 students, but the list was getting updated. My name wasn’t there in
the initial list they sent but later on my name was added in the list so I became ready for
the MR round.
Around 30 students were shortlisted for MR round
Round 3: Managerial Interview (15-20 minutes)
This round will be taken by a senior manager in the company. My interview started off with
my introduction, in my intro, in the last I mentioned my hobbies as reading mythology so
he asked me what material I have read, he had probably read it too so we had a small
discussion on it. Then, he asked me whether I am from mumbai; I am from Pune, so I told
him the same, he was probably taking the interview from his residence which  was the area
neighbouring mine so he was like okay then we are neighbours. This discussion kind of
made me comfortable as it seemed to be a very friendly environment. Then he started
4

asking me questions from my resume. He asked me one question based on my internship. I
actually hadn’t covered that part in depth during my internship so I just told him that I
hadn’t touched that topic in detail. In such situations, always be honest and tell them
whatever you know. Then he noticed that I had done 2 projects and a competition which
were all team projects, so he started asking me situation based questions. He asked me
what I would do if for some reason few members of the team aren’t able to contribute to
the project. I told him I would first try to speak to the members who aren’t contributing, try
to know their reason of not being active, if there is some misunderstanding or problems
they are facing then as a leader, it's my responsibility to solve them and make them
comfortable working with the team, but if there are genuine problems then probably I
would redistribute the tasks and see if other members of the group can take up the
responsibility, and if others too are not capable of completing the tasks (i.e if there is some
task which is very skill specific and only people with that skill set will be able to complete
that task) then, I’ll look for a replacement which is the last resort. This was more of a
discussion kind of thing, I mean I would say some point and the interviewer would cross
question me and help me improve my answer. I also gave him an example as I had
experienced this situation in one of my projects. In situation based questions, often real life
experiences help us explain things better, so if you have one then take help of that. Then
he asked me to explain the different phases of building a project (basically SRS, planning,
risk estimation, development (coding), testing and deployment). He then went into software
life cycle models and asked a few questions on that, not very specific to the subject but the
general ones. Then he asked me to describe a situation where I was responsible for
completion of an agenda, that is I had taken that task to completion. I answered that and
he seemed to be satisfied. Then he asked me if I had any certifications, I mentioned the
recent and major ones. There were a few questions that he asked which I was not able to
answer. I remember one of the questions, he asked me that once you build an application,
you need to ensure that it works the desired way on all sorts of devices (IOS device, an
android device etc) so how do you test your code for that. I answered something, but it
wasn’t what he probably expected. I told him that I haven't had enough experience with
this, he was like okay you atleast are honest enough to tell me that. Then, he asked me
whether I had any questions for him.
ALWAYS ASK QUESTIONS.
5

It shows them your interest in their company. After my technical round, I had some 1-1.5
hrs. Since I thought I might get selected in the next round, as my technical round didn’t go
that bad, I utilized the time in between to research about the company. I collected 4
questions to ask the interviewer out of which 2 of them were very specific to their company
(like I went through their official website and I asked them about a payment solution they
had recently launched) and the other 2 were general questions. I think, not sure though,
that he really liked my questions as it reflected that I am keen towards working with them.
In the end, I apologized as the 15 minutes interview lasted for more than 25 minutes,
probably due to my questions :/
He said you should always ask questions and it is good that you had so many questions to
ask. He told me that I could even connect with them on linkedIn and ask any further
questions there.
23 of us were offered the internship.
The company took a very long time (4 days) to declare the results :/
Preparation Tips
-
Fiserv is a company which won't go very deep into Coding aspects, according to my
experience. They are more interested in judging your analytical approaches, also,
they are keen to see your extracurricular activities.
-
There are 2 things you must keep ready- Introduction and Questions to ask to the
interviewer.
-
It is perfectly normal to encounter a question that you are unaware of or haven’t
revised.  If a particular concept is known and you don’t recall it, just tell them that
you have studied this particular topic but you aren’t able to recall it now and that
you’ll have to brush up and if it is an unknown question, just don’t become hesitated
to say that you don’t know, at the same time, don’t just give up, try answering it upto
the extent you can. Sometimes they purposely ask such questions to test your grit.
So, always try your level best to answer each and every question.
-
KNOW YOUR RESUME INSIDE OUT. They can pick up any small thing and start asking
questions on that, so be prepared for questions on every single thing you have
6

mentioned on your resume. Keep your resume authentic, don’t write any false
things to just fill up the resume, if they ask questions you might get into problem
-
If you don’t understand their question, don’t hesitate to ask them to repeat the
question.
-
Even if you are unable to answer a question, don’t become tensor nervous, in MR
kind of rounds, many times they purposely ask questions to judge your behaviour
and or body language in such under pressure situations.
-
Lastly, be confident and keep a smile on your face throughout. Don’t consider it to
be an interview, think of it like a discussion with your friend if you become too
anxious.

Honestly, before the interview, I didn’t think mera fiserv me hoga, so I continued with my
preparation. I thought of this interview as an opportunity to cover some topics I had to
revise and it indeed helped me in my interview. So, I think you should consider each
interview test/interview as an opportunity to make yourselves better and finally, it will pay
off in some or the other company surely.
Finally,
Tension mat lo, ho jayega. Just keep the preparation on :)
ALL THE BEST!!!
